description.narrative: It is necessary for the Croix-Rouge centrafricaine (CRCA) to conduct a self-assessment based on the Preparedness for Effective Response (PER) methodology (in French: "Préparation pour une Intervention Efficace (PIE)". The PIE is a cyclical approach allowing the Société Nationale (SN) to systematically evaluate, measure and analyze the strengths and weaknesses of its intervention system in order to take corrective measures. It is this PIE process that will be the heart of the conception phase of the RP 3 project, followed by an implementation phase.

The PER approach which will be put in place during the conception phase, which consists of assessing the full capacities of the National Society to prepare and respond to disasters, identifying the priority areas of focus to be strengthened and establishing a plan of action with detailed activities. To achieve this, the work will be organised in 5 phases: the orientation phase (already done under RPII but a new one is needed to refresh minds and rebuild a momentum), the assessment phase, the prioritization and analysis phase, the work plan phase and the action and accountability phase. The project to be implemented with this funding will mainly be designed as a contribution to the PER workplan. Therefore, the PER process will enable the CRCA to determine the focus of this project, once the PER 3rd and 4th phases are completed. The priorities that came out of the PER approach are: Rôle auxiliaire, mandat et législation de la CR; Qualité et responsabilité; Procédures d'intervention d'urgence (SOPs); Premiers secours; Santé à base communautaire; Evaluation des besoins d'urgence. In addition, and to ensure that the CRCA has minimum capacities for the coming rainy seasons, some basic floods preparedness activities will be carried out as early as possible.
Lastly, this project will also be an opportunity to contribute to developing the capacities of the CRCA to implement cash-based programming. To ensure that enough time is allocated to this effort, cash-based programming strengthening activities will start as soon as possible, potentially in collaboration with the IFRC.

There is a need to reform National Disaster Response Teams and Community Disaster Response Teams while readapting the training approach with more in (on-site) actions and enhanced monitoring from headquarters to branches through regular visits and supervision during their activities in the field.
